newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's BNL, INA to bid for BancoNapoli.
newsitem.headline: Italy's BNL, INA to bid for BancoNapoli.

text.p: Italy's Banca Nazionale del Lavoro (BNL) said on Thursday it had decided along with insurer INA to offer to buy 60 percent of struggling southern Banco di Napoli.
BNL said in a statement the board had mandated chairman Marco Sarcinelli and managing director Davide Croff to arrange the offer.
INA said on Tuesday a board meeting had authorised its executives to prepare an offer to buy a 60 percent stake in Banco di Napoli together with BNL.
The Italian Treasury took temporary control of Banco di Napoli, Italy's largest southern bank, after it unveiled record losses of 3.12 trillion lire ($2.0 billion) in 1995.
The bank plunged a further 674 billion lire into the red in the first half of this year and the Treasury has given interested parties until December 20 to make offers.
The Treasury said on Tuesday it had kicked off a 1.977 trillion lire capital increase for the ailing bank, beginning the underwriting for the operation. $1=1,530
